about: Curated knowledge-graph layer for /ai+science/. Reading-list entries in ai-science.json become resource nodes automatically, and their tags become topic nodes. This file adds the people, organisations, venues, concepts, methods and artifacts around them. Relations have a label and an inverse label (shown on the target node). Edges are [source, relation, target] and may carry a fourth element as a short note. Run python3 scripts/build_ai_science.py after editing.

nodes.label: AGMAI
nodes.description: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence.

nodes.label: Fields medallists’ letter
nodes.description: An open letter from Fields medallists on AI and mathematics, discussed by Gowers.

nodes.label: Verification as the bottleneck
nodes.description: As producing results gets cheaper, checking them and owning responsibility for them becomes the scarce resource.

nodes.label: Understanding vs. answers
nodes.description: The value of science lies partly in humans understanding results, not only in results existing.

nodes.label: Research taste
nodes.description: Judgment about which questions and directions are worth pursuing.

nodes.label: Credit and provenance
nodes.description: Who did the work, where ideas and data came from, and who is accountable.

nodes.label: Scientific institutions
nodes.description: Journals, prizes, departments and communities that sustain shared understanding.

nodes.label: Uncertainty records
nodes.description: Machine-reusable qualifications attached to scientific claims.

nodes.label: Autonomous research agents
nodes.description: Pipelines where AI systems plan, run and write up research with little human input.

nodes.label: Multi-agent coordination
nodes.description: How teams or swarms of agents divide labour, communicate and check each other.

nodes.label: Verifier exploits and reward hacking
nodes.description: Agents gaming the checker instead of solving the problem; can spread through shared infrastructure.

nodes.label: Test-time scaling
nodes.description: Spending more compute at inference: longer reasoning, parallel exploration, latent iteration.

nodes.label: Formalization of proofs
nodes.description: Turning human proofs into machine-checked proofs.

nodes.label: Measurement and causal biology
nodes.description: Better data about human biology as the real constraint on AI drug discovery.

nodes.label: Inspectable scientific reasoning
nodes.description: Representations and interfaces that let people see and challenge how a conclusion was reached.

nodes.label: Implementation drift
nodes.description: Agents silently changing the experiment they were asked to run.

nodes.label: Decision-relevant evaluation
nodes.description: Judging AI by whether it improves real decisions and outcomes, not benchmark scores.

nodes.label: Selection effects in reported wins
nodes.description: Showcased successes may be cherry-picked from many attempts.

nodes.label: Learned coordination strategies
nodes.description: Frozen models learning reusable ways to coordinate as a team.

nodes.label: The Agentic Scientist
nodes.description: Sakana's scaffold that orchestrates coding agents through hypothesis, rubric-based evaluation, shared memory and ablation stages.

nodes.label: The AI Scientist (v1, v2)
nodes.description: Sakana's earlier end-to-end automated research systems, the predecessors of the Agentic Scientist.

nodes.label: Coding agents (Codex, Claude Code)
nodes.description: Agents that carry out long software tasks on their own.

nodes.label: AutoIllustrate
nodes.description: A pipeline for scientific figures that keeps an editable draw.io file as the source of truth, so every diagram can be corrected by hand.

nodes.label: Co-discovery
nodes.description: Humans set the question and the standards of evidence, and agents widen the experiments researchers can run.

nodes.label: Optimizer, not scientist
nodes.description: Coding agents given a research problem tend to push scores up with narrow ideas, without examining why the gains happen.

nodes.label: Error Diffusion
nodes.description: A biologically motivated alternative to backpropagation.

nodes.label: Pre-registered rubrics
nodes.description: Evaluation criteria fixed before any experiment runs.

nodes.label: Parallel workers with shared memory
nodes.description: Workers test hypotheses in parallel and pool successes and failures.

nodes.label: ICLR 2025 ICBINB workshop
nodes.description: The “I Can’t Believe It’s Not Better” workshop, where an AI Scientist-v2 paper averaged 6.33 in blind review.

nodes.label: Automated Reviewer
nodes.description: An ensemble of five LLM reviews following NeurIPS guidelines, reported at 69% balanced accuracy on OpenReview decisions.

nodes.label: Norms for AI-generated papers
nodes.description: Watermarking, disclosure, withdrawal and IRB review for research written by AI.

nodes.label: Agents4Science 2025
nodes.description: A venue that required AI first authors.

nodes.label: Agent_H
nodes.description: A medical-QA agent architecture found by a fully autonomous search in the Gemini real-world study.

nodes.label: ATHENA
nodes.description: A treatment-reasoning agent from Zitnik's lab, wired to disease data, patient cohorts and FDA drug records.

nodes.label: Google Co-Scientist
nodes.description: Started as an idea-generation system and was extended into an ideation, experimentation and paper-writing pipeline.

nodes.label: Goodhart’s law
nodes.description: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.

nodes.label: Eureka instinct
nodes.description: Agents declaring success too early and writing up results with too much excitement.

nodes.label: Proof indigestion
nodes.description: Results arriving faster than people can absorb and understand them.

nodes.label: Knowledge-commons governance
nodes.description: An Ostrom-style framing: shared libraries need sanctions and collective choice, not only visibility.

nodes.label: Institutions as design primitives
nodes.description: Building roles, rules and enforcement into multi-agent systems rather than treating agents as lone optimizers.

nodes.label: Solipsistic AI
nodes.description: Assuming a fixed, stationary world in which the AI is the only optimizer.

nodes.label: Fabrication under LLM review
nodes.description: Agents optimized against an LLM reviewer learn to invent results.

nodes.label: Fast, cheap feedback
nodes.description: AI wins come where scorecards are fast and cheap. Clinical outcomes are neither.

nodes.label: Context of use and proxy validity
nodes.description: Whether a measured proxy predicts the human outcome that matters.

nodes.label: Deskilling
nodes.description: Human skills atrophying when work is handed to AI.

nodes.label: Demonstrability
nodes.description: How easily a correct answer can be shown to be correct.

nodes.label: Physical experimentation bottleneck
nodes.description: Wet labs, furnaces and characterization stay slow while analysis gets cheap.

nodes.label: Deterministic claim-to-log checks
nodes.description: Every number in a write-up is checked against execution logs.

nodes.label: Step audits and divergence reconciliation
nodes.description: Teammates flag the specific step where they disagree, and the step is re-checked by agents that did not write it.

nodes.label: Discovery Loop
nodes.description: A Palo Alto public benefit corporation launched on 5 Aug 2026 to automate ML, science and engineering experiments.

nodes.label: Experimental loop latency
nodes.description: Cutting the time per propose, implement, run and evaluate cycle to minutes or hours, and running thousands of cycles in parallel.

nodes.label: Recursive self-improvement
nodes.description: Using AI research tools to improve the stack that builds them.

nodes.label: NAE Grand Challenges
nodes.description: The US National Academy of Engineering’s 14 grand challenges, such as medicines, clean water and solar.

nodes.label: Context graphs
nodes.description: Prebuilt graphs of the entities and relations in a document collection, handed to agents as structured context instead of raw text.

nodes.label: Verifiable hill-climbing
nodes.description: Change, test, repeat until a programmatic goal is met. Models already excel at this.

nodes.label: Regression to the mean in open-ended choices
nodes.description: Without a verifier, model choices drift toward the familiar and average, so they are functional but generic.

nodes.label: Jev (TypeSafe)
nodes.description: A small “System One” model that answers typed questions with calibrated probabilities in about 150 ms.

nodes.label: Decision/action split
nodes.description: A model classifies what something is; deterministic code decides what happens next. From 12-Factor Agents.

nodes.label: Agent writes its own workflow
nodes.description: An agent does a task from an SOP, then compiles what it learned into a typed workflow that handles most cases without it.

nodes.label: Replayable, per-node evaluation
nodes.description: Re-run each judgment without redoing the research, and score every workflow step on its own.

nodes.label: Drug discovery and biopharma
nodes.description: Using AI across the drug pipeline, from target biology and R&D to clinical, regulatory and commercial work.

nodes.label: Penalty-based rubric grading
nodes.description: Experts list the errors a work product must avoid, weighted major, moderate or minor; an LLM grader applies the checklist with citations.

nodes.label: Synthesis vs compilation gap
nodes.description: Models compile structured trackers well but do worse at integrating evidence into narrative judgments.

nodes.label: Experiment portfolio by expected value per cost
nodes.description: Score each queued experiment by expected value divided by its compute and other costs, and run the best first.

nodes.label: The 10x signal
nodes.description: A 10x gain in compute-to-quality marks an idea as important, as with mixture of experts.

nodes.label: The 5-of-7 problem shape
nodes.description: Good research problems have most parts starting to take shape and a few hard but imaginable, on about a 5-year horizon.

nodes.label: The shared science–engineering loop
nodes.description: Decompose, propose, implement, evaluate, feed back, repeat.

nodes.label: Reliability as institutional design
nodes.description: When AI systems become many communicating agents, reliability may depend as much on the rules of the collective as on aligning each model.

nodes.label: Governed claim ledger
nodes.description: Shared claims are reviewed, promoted, challenged and corrected under explicit rules. Detecting a problem is kept separate from the authority to change the record, and repairs are scoped: narrow, downgrade, reassess or revoke.

nodes.label: Typed scientific knowledge objects
nodes.description: Shared memory as claims, hypotheses, evidence, contradictions, negative results, replications, retractions and uncertainty, like PubMed plus Git plus peer review, not a chat log.

nodes.label: Selective contagion of ideas
nodes.description: Treat claims like infections: keep R below 1 for bad claims and well above 1 for validated ones. Heuristic: detection, adjudication and intervention must be faster than a harmful claim spreads.

nodes.label: Separated evidence chain
nodes.description: Prediction quality, specification fidelity, decision utility and clinical translation are kept apart. In biology, association, intervention, mechanism and translation are separate stages, and evidence for one does not validate the next.

nodes.label: Integrity reporting channels
nodes.description: Separate channels for negative results, uncertainty reports, confessions, pre-action alerts and peer challenges, each with its own response, so that reporting disappointing science is not punished.

nodes.label: Protected distinct bets
nodes.description: Give cohorts of agents protected budgets to pursue different hypotheses. Compare diversity on complete proposals against repeated sampling from one strong model at the same budget.

nodes.label: Benchling Science Foundries
nodes.description: Agent teams that run a lab process end to end on shared data, with scientist approval steps chosen by the team.

nodes.label: Scientist approval gates
nodes.description: Assign each workflow step to an agent or a person, and require a scientist's sign-off at chosen decision points.

nodes.label: Idea basins
nodes.description: Long-running agents stay in a local region of solution space and refine their own earlier ideas, so independent runs end far apart.

nodes.label: Anchoring on history
nodes.description: As an agent's context grows, its proposals become smaller and more conservative.

nodes.label: Fork-and-flush
nodes.description: Periodically fork into fresh-context trajectories that keep the workspace, then continue from the best.

nodes.label: Forgetting (keep only the best)
nodes.description: Periodically discard all sessions and search state, keeping only the best candidate, and restart fresh agents from it.

nodes.label: Autoresearch agents
nodes.description: Agents that loop propose, score and refine on a measurable research or engineering task, as in Karpathy's autoresearch.

nodes.label: VERID
nodes.description: A semantic digital twin of a lab workcell that dry-runs and safety-checks robot protocols.

nodes.label: PyLabRobot
nodes.description: Open-source framework for controlling lab robots.

nodes.label: Digital-twin dry runs
nodes.description: Simulate every protocol against a live model of the lab before any physical action.

nodes.label: Aptamer lab-in-the-loop
nodes.description: Pooled synthesis and sequencing readout give a 7–10 day design–test–analyze cycle.

nodes.label: Epitope excision
nodes.description: Re-fold only the local binding pocket of a large target to cut structure-prediction cost.

nodes.label: Biosecurity screening of designs
nodes.description: Every designed sequence is screened before synthesis.

nodes.label: Human strategy, agent tactics
nodes.description: The scientist chooses where to aim; the agent executes and iterates within that choice.
